stem: A client who is stable on warfarin begins an antibiotic. What should the nurse anticipate regarding anticoagulation monitoring?

options.A: More frequent INR monitoring while the antibiotic is started or stopped.
options.B: No added INR monitoring because antibiotics do not alter warfarin response.
options.C: Automatic doubling of the warfarin dose during antibiotic treatment.
options.D: Automatic discontinuation of warfarin for every antibiotic course.

rationale: Warfarin labeling states that antibiotics and antifungals can be associated with changes in INR and directs clinicians to closely monitor INR when an antibiotic or antifungal is started or stopped. The effect is not reliably in one direction, so dose changes should be based on measured response rather than automatic adjustment. A is correct.
educational_objective: Recognize the need for closer INR monitoring when antibiotics are started or stopped in a client taking warfarin.
source_locator: Drug Interactions, section 7.3 — Antibiotics and Antifungals
source_claim_supported: Closely monitor INR when starting or stopping an antibiotic or antifungal in patients taking warfarin.

source_original.stem: A client stable on warfarin starts an antibiotic. What is the safest nursing expectation regarding anticoagulation monitoring?

options.A: Start closer INR monitoring because antibiotics can alter warfarin effect and bleeding risk
options.B: Continue warfarin unchanged without added INR checks because antibiotics do not interact
options.C: Double the warfarin dose during antibiotic therapy to prevent inadequate anticoagulation
options.D: Automatically stop warfarin for every antibiotic course regardless of INR or indication

source_original.rationale: Antibiotics and the infection itself can alter warfarin response, and specific anti-infectives may raise or lower INR through different mechanisms. The safe response is closer INR and bleeding/thrombosis monitoring with dose adjustment based on measured response rather than assuming a uniform direction of interaction.
source_original.source_detail: Drug interactions/monitoring: interacting anti-infectives may alter anticoagulant response; INR should be monitored more closely when interacting drugs are started or stopped; accessed 2026-08-14.

correction_summary: Replaced the DailyMed search page with a specific label and exact section 7.3 locator, removed unsupported generalization about infection itself, and reduced difficulty from hard to medium.

audit_findings.claim_audit: Section 7.3 directly requires close INR monitoring when antibiotics are started or stopped.
audit_findings.ambiguity_second_answer: A is the only response consistent with labeled monitoring guidance.
audit_findings.blueprint: Drug interaction monitoring fits Pharmacological and Parenteral Therapies.
audit_findings.independent_second_pass: Rechecked section 7.3; no second defensible answer.
